drinksPackage.perDayBasis: MANDATORY service charge for the BEVERAGE perk only. It does NOT prepay daily gratuities, and — CORRECTED 18 Aug 2026 — it does NOT cover the specialty dining perk either. This field previously read "Single combined MANDATORY service charge covering the Unlimited Open Bar AND the Specialty Dining perk", which was wrong and understated every NCL estimate by the dining fee. NCL bills the two perks separately, each under its own heading with its own price table and its own liability sentence: "Guests are responsible for the cost of the Unlimited Open Bar and Soda [Package] prior to their cruise" under Beverage Package Pricing, and "Guests are responsible for the ADDITIONAL cost of the Specialty Dining Package prior to their cruise" under Specialty Dining Package. The dining price lives in drinksPackage.specialtyDiningCharge. Evidence: docs/price-changes/2026-08-18-ncl-specialty-dining-charge.md. VERIFIED FIRST-PARTY 3 Aug 2026 against the NCL MIAMI promotions terms — the edition whose own scope line reads "Applicable to NCL MIAMI, NCL INTL, NCL AUSTRALIA, NCL BRAZIL and NCL ASIA / Not applicable to NCL MEA, NCL GERMANY/CE or NCL UK offices". That distinction matters: the CE/UK edition served to European visitors prices Free at Sea as a per-person upgrade fee instead and explicitly excludes NCL Miami, which is why two earlier verification attempts failed. Beverage Package Pricing table, verbatim: 2-5 Nights $32.00 USD, 6+ Nights $28.50 USD, "Price in USD Per Person"; per-day confirmed by the same document ("Unlimited Pop Beverage Package is $12.50 USD per person per day", Hawaii package "$28.50 per person per day") and by ncl.com FAQ ("Starting at $28.50 per guest per day"). specialtyDiningCharge.note: Free at Sea specialty dining is an ADDITIONAL charge, separate from the beverage service charge in perDay. NCL US terms, verbatim: "Guests are responsible for the additional cost of the Specialty Dining Package prior to their cruise", under a Specialty Dining Package heading and price table distinct from Beverage Package Pricing. Charged PER ELIGIBLE GUEST for the whole voyage, guests 1-2 only. The meal count is written at reservation level, but the FEE is unambiguously per guest: a second guest aged 2-12 on the kids' menu "will not be charged the specialty dining package fee", and one aged 13 or older pays "the standard Free at Sea specialty dining package fee". Owner ruling 18 Aug 2026: two adults on a 7-night sailing pay the 7-8 band twice. FREE AT SEA PLUS PAYS IT TOO — checked, not assumed: the Plus prepaid service charge "does not cover bar and beverage service charges, specialty dining gratuities, spa services", and the Plus dining benefit is 50% off ADDITIONAL covers only. So it attaches on both tiers and does not move the Free at Sea vs Plus comparison. Ages are not modelled (standing scope decision), so the calculator charges min(guests, 2); a stateroom whose second guest is a child eating from the kids' menu is overstated by one fee, which is the conservative direction.
specialtyDiningCharge.source: NCL US promotions terms, Specialty Dining Package pricing table, captured 18 Aug 2026 from https://www.ncl.com/cruise-deals/promotion-terms#free-at-sea (PDF sha256 bea97f0ed5418f46964a637e4c2ef99ceaaf70afc1f17057a029a417a23626ed). Full working: docs/price-changes/2026-08-18-ncl-specialty-dining-charge.md.

standaloneAvailability.note: NCL publishes NO separately purchasable price for its alcohol package. Its own beverage-packages page prices only the Unlimited Soda and Unlimited Starbucks packages; against every alcohol package it says only that "an additional cost will be added to your booking for this optional upgrade selection". The open bar is branded "Free at Sea Premium Beverage Package" and NCL states it is the only adult beverage package it offers. Where a figure IS quoted it is a RETAIL VALUE — the base NCL applies a percentage to, per its own wording "20% gratuity and beverage service charge on the retail value of the package" — not a shelf price. CruiseClarify therefore compares the mandatory charge a guest actually pays (perDay / shortSailingPerDay) against expected pay-as-you-go spending, and quotes no standalone price. Pride of America is a genuinely separate product (Free at Sea Hawaii Beverage Package), not a price variant of this one.
standaloneAvailability.verify: Retired figures, kept here only so they are recognisable if they resurface: the record previously asserted $89/day + 20% = ~$106.80, with "$109 base on Pride of America only". Live pages also carried $109 + 20% (implying $130.80). None is a price a guest can pay; $89 is additionally stale. Secondary 2026 sources put the current retail VALUE near $109 — not recorded as a number here because CruiseClarify neither publishes nor computes from it. Articles still quoting these figures are corrected in a later phase (TD-014).

specialtyDining.note: Free at Sea includes a fixed number of specialty dining meals set by sailing length — NCL: "Number of meals depends on the length of the cruise." A COUNT for the whole voyage, not a nightly allowance, so no per-night value can represent it. Meals beyond the entitlement are charged at the venue cover (see specialtyDining.range); NCL: "Anything consumed above the promotional benefit will be the responsibility of the guest at prevailing rates." Free at Sea Plus adds 50% off those extra covers. Stated in full, valued at nothing.
specialtyDining.verify: PARTLY RESOLVED 3 Aug 2026 (NCL MIAMI terms). SETTLED: the package is "Applicable to guests 1-2 on the reservation" and "applicable to guests ages 2 and older" — so guests 3-8 receive none, and TD-014.2 (age) is closed. STILL UNRESOLVED, AND THE REASON NO MULTIPLIER IS RECORDED: NCL never states that EACH of guests 1 and 2 receives the published count. It states who the package applies to, and separately how many meals the package contains. Two pieces of evidence point AWAY from doubling: (a) its dining price column is headed "Pre-Purchase Price (gratuities included)" with NO "Per Person" qualifier, where the Beverage Package Pricing table immediately above it explicitly says "Price in USD Per Person"; (b) the second-guest clause reads "up to the amount of nights THE RESERVATION is entitled to", which frames the entitlement at reservation level. Until NCL says otherwise, no renderer may multiply the count by guests. Source: docs/price-changes/2026-08-03-ncl-us-terms/full-text.md. SUPERSEDED NOTES FOLLOW: (1) whether the meal count is per ELIGIBLE GUEST or per stateroom — NCL's table says only "Meals". The offer is priced per person and the Wi-Fi line specifies "1 login per guest", which points to per guest, and CruiseClarify's own NCL article already says "per person" — but NCL does not state it for dining, so no basis flag is recorded here and no renderer may assume one. (2) whether any age restriction applies (the beverage component is 21+; dining is not stated). (3) whether the entitlement differs by cabin grade or fare type — Suite/Haven receive the same component set under a different promo code, but this is not confirmed for the US market. Resolve before any renderer multiplies this count by guests. TD-014.

shoreExcursion.note: Free at Sea grants a $50 shore-excursion credit. NCL MIAMI terms, verbatim: "A $50 Shore Excursion Credit is available for each port of call on the voyage", and "The first guest may apply the $50 credit per port to one or multiple eligible excursions within the same port." FIRST GUEST ONLY — "Other guests in the same stateroom are not eligible" and the credit "may not be applied to purchases for other guests". PER PORT, not per excursion, and it may be split across several excursions in the same port. NO ROLL-OVER: "If the cost of an eligible excursion is less than $50, the unused value is forfeited. No cash value or substitute credit will be issued." Redeemable only against NCL-booked excursions, so it is worth nothing to a guest who explores independently. STATED AND NEVER DEDUCTED: `deducted` is false, and treating a restricted credit as cash would overstate the package exactly as ignoring it understates it.
shoreExcursion.verify: RESOLVED 3 Aug 2026 against the NCL MIAMI terms (TD-014.3 closed): per port not per excursion; may be split across multiple excursions within the same port; does NOT roll over; first guest only; not refundable, not transferable, no cash value. ONE CONFLICT NOTED AND RESOLVED BY HIERARCHY: NCL's own flyer (FASvsFAS+_Flyer_4.26.pdf) says "$50 credit per tour", which the terms contradict with the per-port wording above. Terms outrank the flyer. STILL OPEN: nothing. Source: docs/price-changes/2026-08-03-ncl-us-terms/full-text.md.

THE VALUATION RULE, which is an AVOIDED COST and not the price of what Plus includes: Plus includes MedallionNet MAX for one device, and Max is not sold separately, so it has no retail price and is given none. What a Plus buyer demonstrably avoids is buying the cheapest separately purchasable plan — Classic, one device — which is this record's own published wifi.perDay. That published rate is therefore credited, and Max's superior service is worth more than the credit but is deliberately assigned NO extra value. Conservative by construction: it can understate Plus, never overstate it. SCOPE: this rule is written for the PLUS one-device entitlement. This ONE object serves both tiers, so Premier is credited the same $25 — Premier's four-device Max entitlement is NOT valued at the $45 four-device Classic plan, because no owner ruling has approved that and Premier's own article states the extra devices are convenience rather than avoided spending. Premier is therefore understated here, in the same safe direction. PREMIER includes UNLIMITED casual and specialty dining, which cannot be priced without assuming how often the traveller eats there.
